Treat each `Iff` as an equivalence between two independently true statements: prove both sides unconditionally, then build each implication by ignoring its hypothesis.

- For the first `Iff`, use the standard identification
  \[
  Z_1(G)=Z(G)
  \]
  for the first upper central-series term. The other side is Dirichlet’s theorem on infinitely many primes in a reduced residue class, applied using `q ≠ 0` and `Coprime a q`.

- For the second `Iff`, evaluate both sides separately. For the cyclotomic assertion, express the field norm of \(\zeta_p-1\) as the product over its conjugates, hence as the cyclotomic polynomial evaluated at \(1\):
  \[
  N_{L/K}(1-\zeta_p)=\Phi_p(1)=p.
  \]
  Since \(p\) is prime and \(p\ne2\), \(p\) is odd and \(p-1\) is even, so replacing \(1-\zeta_p\) by \(\zeta_p-1\) introduces no sign. Irreducibility ensures that the conjugates/minimal polynomial give the full norm.

- For the series, split by parity using
  \[
  \sin(\pi n/2)=
  \begin{cases}
  0,&n\text{ even},\\
  (-1)^k,&n=2k+1,
  \end{cases}
  \]
  reducing it to the Dirichlet beta value
  \[
  \sum_{k\ge0}\frac{(-1)^k}{(2k+1)^3}
  =\beta(3)=\frac{\pi^3}{32}.
  \]
  Establish the corresponding unconditional `HasSum`, then assemble the second `Iff` in the same hypothesis-ignoring way.

The only materially important obstruction is \(p=2\): the sign in \(N(\zeta_p-1)\) would not disappear.
